title: Normal verifications of intuitionistic propositional proofs

based_on.title: Proofs and Types (web reprint 2003, corrected 1990 edition)
Constructive Logic: Cut Elimination (Lecture 10, October 5, 2017; edits by Andre Platzer)

summary: Reconstruct intuitionistic sequent proofs as normal natural-deduction verifications, track their formulas, and extract theorem disjuncts from their final constructors.
abstract: An implication may be proved and then immediately used, leaving an avoidable detour in a deduction. We distinguish proofs that introduce a conclusion from uses that follow an available assumption through elimination rules. Every intuitionistic propositional theorem has a proof in this normal shape, constructed through cut-free sequents. The construction also handles disjunction by keeping later uses inside its branches. Its formula trace uses only subformulas of the conclusion and assumptions, with falsum tracked explicitly, and a closed disjunction proof reveals a proof of one of its disjuncts.
